principles.text: Most SEO fails because it is spread too thin, not because it is bad. Put the effort on one money keyword and one page.
People do not pay to know, they pay for the thing to exist. Build tools that end in a finished output, not a report.
Paid traffic is rented attention and stops when you stop paying. Content published once keeps producing traffic.
Writing the article is not enough. One well-distributed article will outperform ten undistributed ones.
Pay for links on pages already in the top 10-20 for bottom-of-funnel keywords. They send referral traffic and AI citations.

sampleQA.question: How do I get ChatGPT to recommend my SaaS?

answer.text: Ask AI for the best tools in your category, paste the competitors it names into Ahrefs, and find the "Best X" listicles linking to them. Then email those authors.
Offer to pay for placement in listicles AI already cites. Leading with "your article is cited by AI" gets replies.
Do not block all AI bots in robots.txt. Keep search and answer bots such as OAI-SearchBot and ChatGPT-User, or you lose those citations.
Small sites can still help, because you do not need a high domain rating to appear in AI search.

sampleQA.question: How much should I pay for a backlink?

answer.text: The median guest post on DR 30+ sites is $100, and the median stays flat from DR 30 to DR 59, so do not pay DR 60 prices for DR 50 sites.
Check organic traffic before DR: 43% of DR 30+ sites get under 1,000 monthly visits.
Spend the most on pages already ranking top 10-20 for your keywords. He pays up to $1,000-$2,000 for those.
Skip very cheap links. Google may ignore them, and a link on a spam network can hurt you.

sampleQA.question: How do I reduce churn on a low-priced SaaS?

answer.text: Split churn by type (voluntary, involuntary, bad-fit, activation, value) before choosing a fix, and keep trials and failed payments out of the same number as serious customers.
Get users to one real outcome with as few choices as possible, and send recaps of what they achieved so they remember the value before renewal.
Push annual plans with discounts and extras, because sunk cost makes those users extract more value. Automate dunning, since manual follow-up on failed payments costs too much at low ARPA.
Check the price itself. Sometimes the fix is removing the plan that invites the wrong customer, not offering a discount.
